description.en: ForestBench evaluates multi-agent collaboration by representing MAS traces as unified collaboration graphs, comparing them against query-specific reference forests of successful graphs, and scoring structural similarity with a metric panel.

attentionForecast.reason: The structural evaluation approach could interest multi-agent researchers, but the absence of an explicit code or data link in the supplied evidence may slow initial adoption.

curation.canonicalNameEvidence: Instantiating the framework as ForestBench, we filter $844$ collaboration-necessary queries from seven public datasets, precompute ten successful target-conditioned reference graphs per query, and evaluate six representative MAS frameworks.
curation.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed set of filtered queries, precomputed reference forests, and a deterministic scoring protocol; it is reusable as a public evaluation framework even though the paper does not currently list a separate artifact link.

evidence.snippet: Each forest is a benchmark-provided collection of verified-success graphs: it records diverse ways in which representative MAS methods can complete the task, rather than prescribing a unique optimal process.

claire_radar.motivation: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on Large Language Models (LLMs) are proliferating rapidly, but their heterogeneous execution traces provide no common basis for evaluation across methods.
